_comment: Signatures produced by verusd 1.2.17-2 on VRSCTEST, used to reverse-engineer and then pin the VerusID message-signing scheme. Reproduced by crates/verus-tx/src/signature.rs.

_scheme.signedHash: SHA256( compactSize(19) || 'Verus signed data:\n' || systemID(20) || blockHeight(4 LE) || identityID(20) || msgHash(32) )
_scheme.signature: header(27 + recid + 4 if compressed) || r(32) || s(32)
_scheme.wire: version(1) || blockHeight(4 LE) || compactSize(count) || [ compactSize(65) || sig(65) ]...
_scheme._note: Single SHA256 at both stages, not the double-SHA256 used for txids and sighashes.

vectors._why: empty: catches a length prefix that was skipped entirely
a second message at the same height, so the height is not the only thing varying
300 bytes: the only vector that distinguishes a compact size from a single length byte

_reverse_direction._comment: The other direction was checked live: a signature this SDK produced was accepted by verifymessage on api.verustest.net for flow1167608@, and rejected for a modified challenge. See crates/verus-flows/tests/live_flows.rs.
